newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Bancorex one-month interest rates up again.
newsitem.headline: Romania Bancorex one-month interest rates up again.

text.p: Romania's state-owned bank Bancorex said on Wednesday it had raised interest rates on the one-month leu deposits -- the fourth rise this year -- following tough monetary policies aimed to curb inflation.
A statement from the Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA said the annual rate on one-month deposits rose by 30 points to 150 percent from 120 percent starting Wednesday.
Other Bancorex rates were unchanged at an annual 130 percent on three-month and 100 percent on six-month, nine-month and one-year deposits.

Most of Romanian banks have taken repeated steps to raise deposit rates this year after the central bank's drive to soak leu liquidity in excess from the market. The tighter monetary policy triggered a jump of one-week refinancing rate to 426.50 percent last week from 226.35 percent.

Year-on-year inflation was 76.3 percent in January, sharply up from 56.9 percent last December. Inflation is expected to rise in the coming months following liberalisation of fuel, electricity and food prices.
Romanians rushed to sell their hard currency holdings into leu funds and put their money in banks as deposit rates reached attractive levels.
